cards.title: Introduction to Vue Packaging
cards.content:
When developing reusable components or libraries in Vue.js, you need to package them properly so they can be consumed by other projects or published to npm.

Vue CLI and Vite both provide built-in library modes to bundle your code into standard formats like ESM, UMD, and IIFE.

cards.title: Vite Library Mode
cards.content:
Vite makes building libraries extremely easy. You configure your vite.config.js using the build.lib option:

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    lib: {
      entry: resolve(__dirname, 'src/index.js'),
      name: 'MyVueLib',
      fileName: 'my-vue-lib',
    },
    rollupOptions: {
      external: ['vue'],
      output: {
        globals: {
          vue: 'Vue',
        },
      },
    },
  },
});

cards.title: Steps to Publish a Vue Library
cards.content: Put the steps of creating and publishing a Vue library in the correct order:

items.text: Develop your Vue components and create an entry file exporting them.
Configure Vite or Vue CLI library mode in the build configuration.
Run the build script to generate output files in the dist folder.
Test the package locally using 'npm link' or 'yalc'.
Publish the package to the npm registry using 'npm publish'.
